import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from bridge.config import BridgeConfig, ModelRoute
from bridge.state import BridgeState
from bridge.transport.github_issues import GitHubIssuesTransport
from bridge.worker import BridgeWorker


class FakeGitHub:
    is_igor_question = staticmethod(GitHubIssuesTransport.is_igor_question)
    format_response_comment = staticmethod(GitHubIssuesTransport.format_response_comment)

    def __init__(self):
        self.comments = {11: [], 12: []}
        self.responses = {11: [], 12: []}
        self.next_id = 900
        self.fail_after_publish = False
        self.response_lookups = []

    def list_issue_comments(self, issue_number):
        return list(self.comments[issue_number])

    def find_response_comment(self, issue_number, source_comment_id):
        self.response_lookups.append((issue_number, str(source_comment_id)))
        marker = GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker(source_comment_id)
        return next(
            (c for c in self.responses[issue_number] if marker in c["body"]),
            None,
        )

    def create_issue_comment(self, issue_number, body):
        self.next_id += 1
        created = {"id": self.next_id, "body": body}
        self.responses[issue_number].append(created)
        if self.fail_after_publish:
            self.fail_after_publish = False
            raise RuntimeError("simulated lost HTTP response after GitHub accepted POST")
        return created

    def add_question(self, issue_number, comment_id, body, created_at):
        self.comments[issue_number].append({
            "id": comment_id,
            "created_at": created_at,
            "body": body,
            "user": {"login": "igor-user"},
        })


class FakeOllama:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.answer = "A careful model answer."

    def chat(self, model, messages, *, think=None):
        self.calls.append((model, messages, think))
        return type("Result", (), {"content": self.answer})()


class WorkerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.state = BridgeState(Path(self.temp.name) / "state.sqlite3")
        self.addCleanup(self.state.close)
        self.config = BridgeConfig(
            repository="owner/repo",
            token_env="GITHUB_TOKEN",
            igor_username="igor-user",
            ollama_base_url="http://localhost:11434",
            ollama_timeout_seconds=30,
            models=(
                ModelRoute("qwen", 11, "ollama", "qwen35-local:latest", False),
                ModelRoute("gemma", 12, "ollama", "gemma3:4b"),
            ),
        )
        self.github = FakeGitHub()
        self.ollama = FakeOllama()
        self.worker = BridgeWorker(
            config=self.config,
            state=self.state,
            github=self.github,
            ollama=self.ollama,
        )

    def add_question(self, issue=11, comment_id=101, minute="00"):
        self.github.add_question(
            issue, comment_id, f"Question {comment_id}",
            f"2026-11-13T00:{minute}:00Z",
        )

    def test_poll_filters_and_deduplicates_comments(self):
        self.add_question()
        self.github.comments[11].append({
            "id": 102, "created_at": "2026-11-13T00:01:00Z",
            "body": "not Igor", "user": {"login": "someone-else"},
        })
        self.github.comments[11].append({
            "id": 103, "created_at": "2026-11-13T00:02:00Z",
            "body": "bridge response <!-- igor-model-bridge:response-to=88 -->",
            "user": {"login": "igor-user"},
        })
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.poll(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.poll(), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.state.list_items()), 1)

    def test_processes_oldest_question_and_uses_explicit_issue_route(self):
        self.add_question(comment_id=201, minute="02")
        self.add_question(comment_id=202, minute="01")
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.source_comment_id, "202")
        self.assertEqual(result.model_id, "qwen")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "qwen35-local:latest")
        self.assertIs(self.ollama.calls[0][2], False)
        self.assertIn(
            GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker("202"),
            self.github.responses[11][0]["body"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("202").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("201").status, "NEW")

    def test_routes_second_issue_to_its_configured_model(self):
        self.add_question(issue=12, comment_id=301)
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.model_id, "gemma")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "gemma3:4b")
        self.assertIsNone(self.ollama.calls[0][2])

    def test_reconciles_processing_item_without_calling_ollama(self):
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="401", issue_number=11,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:00:00Z", content="Already answered?",
        )
        self.state.mark_processing("401")
        self.github.responses[11].append({
            "id": 940,
            "body": "Already answered.\n\n"
                    + GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker("401"),
        })
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "reconciled")
        self.assertEqual(result.response_comment_id, "940")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("401").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls, [])

    def test_unpublished_interrupted_item_is_retried_before_new_pending_work(self):
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="451", issue_number=11,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:00:00Z", content="Interrupted question",
        )
        self.state.mark_processing("451")
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="452", issue_number=12,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:01:00Z", content="Newer question",
        )

        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.source_comment_id, "451")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "qwen35-local:latest")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("451").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("452").status, "NEW")

    def test_retry_after_lost_post_response_reconciles_without_duplicate(self):
        self.add_question(comment_id=501)
        self.github.fail_after_publish = True
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "lost HTTP response"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.responses[11]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("501").status, "ERROR")

        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "reconciled")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.responses[11]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.ollama.calls), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("501").status, "RESPONDED")

    def test_provider_failure_keeps_question_retryable(self):
        class BrokenOllama:
            def chat(self, model, messages, *, think=None):
                raise RuntimeError("temporary model failure")

        self.worker.ollama = BrokenOllama()
        self.add_question(comment_id=601)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "temporary model failure"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("601").status, "ERROR")
        # ERROR retries must also reconcile the remote marker before inference.
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "temporary model failure"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(
            self.github.response_lookups,
            [(11, "601"), (11, "601")],
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("601").status, "ERROR")

    def test_single_model_run_does_not_touch_other_issue_queue(self):
        self.add_question(issue=11, comment_id=701)
        self.add_question(issue=12, comment_id=702)
        result = self.worker.run_once(model_id="gemma")

        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.issue_number, 12)
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "gemma3:4b")
        self.assertIsNone(self.ollama.calls[0][2])
        self.assertIsNone(self.state.get("701"))
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("702").status, "RESPONDED")

    def test_idle_when_no_igor_questions_exist(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.run_once().status, "idle")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls, [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

[L2]   "content": "# Igor Model Bridge

A small, independent bridge between Igor (ChatGPT) and local AI models served by Ollama.

## Status

**Protocol/state foundation, GitHub Issues transport, explicit model routing, Ollama adapter, sequential Worker, and a safe one-shot CLI Runner are implemented.** A real GitHub-to-Ollama round trip has not yet been run. No shell access, code editing, or Ilan integration is enabled.

## First milestone

Run a local bridge process that reads Igor's discussion messages from model-specific GitHub Issues, routes each Issue to its explicitly configured Ollama model, queues questions FIFO, posts correlated responses, and recovers safely after restart.

## Agreed v0 decisions

- One persistent GitHub Issue per model; interview rounds can use an optional interview_id.
- Explicit model routing; never infer a model from an Issue title.
- FIFO queue; no pending question is discarded when a newer one arrives.
- Sequential model execution.
- Persistent deduplication using GitHub comment IDs and SQLite.
- Restart reconciliation using stable response correlation markers.
- The practical guarantee is idempotent response publication, not exactly-once inference.

## Boundaries

- The user is the final authority.
- The bridge is independent of Ilan.
- First transport: GitHub Issues; first provider: Ollama.
- v0 is discussion-only: no tools, shell, workspace access, code changes, or task execution.
- Secrets stay local; never commit tokens.
- Model memory unloading/optimization is deferred.

## Configuration

Requires Python 3.11+ (standard-library tomllib).

1. Copy config.example.toml to config.toml.
2. Set github.igor_username to the GitHub login used by Igor.
3. Create the persistent model Issues and replace each issue_number = 0 with its real Issue number.
4. Set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable locally. The token is never stored in TOML.
5. Load with load_config("config.toml"). Startup validation rejects missing or duplicate mappings.

The example lists four local Ollama tags from the earlier model shortlist. Verify the exact tags on the machine before using them. For Qwen routes, set `think = false` to disable Thinking for that route; omit the setting for non-Qwen models to preserve their default behavior.

## Ollama adapter

The standard-library adapter sends non-streaming POST requests to /api/chat, always with an explicit model tag and stream=false. It accepts only system/user/assistant messages and returns the assistant text plus available usage/timing metadata. HTTP errors, connection failures, invalid JSON, incomplete responses, and empty model output are surfaced as OllamaError.

Example:

    from bridge.config import load_config
    from bridge.providers.ollama import OllamaChatClient

    config = load_config("config.toml")
    route = config.model_by_id("qwen35-local")
    client = OllamaChatClient(
        base_url=config.ollama_base_url,
        timeout=config.ollama_timeout_seconds,
    )
    result = client.chat(
        route.model_name,
        [{"role": "user", "content": "Give a short self-introduction."}],
        think=route.think,
    )
    print(result.content)

The adapter does not execute tools or access files. It does not check that a model tag is installed; Ollama reports that at request time.

## Current layout

igor-model-bridge/
- config.example.toml
- src/bridge/config.py
- src/bridge/providers/ollama.py
- src/bridge/runner.py
- src/bridge/__main__.py
- src/bridge/protocol.py
- src/bridge/state.py
- src/bridge/transport/github_issues.py
- tests/test_config.py
- tests/test_ollama.py
- tests/test_runner.py
- tests/test_protocol.py
- tests/test_state.py
- tests/test_worker.py
- tests/test_github_issues.py

## Running the bridge (PowerShell)

    $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
    python -m bridge --config config.toml --model-id qwen35-local

Only after reviewing the queued comment IDs, explicitly enable one live response:

    python -m bridge --config config.toml --model-id qwen35-local --execute

Safety properties:
- `--execute` requires an explicit `--model-id`; one run processes at most one item from that model's Issue.
- Other model Issues and their queue items are left untouched during a model-scoped run.
- Without `--execute`, the Runner does not call Ollama or create GitHub comments.
- The GitHub token is read from the configured environment variable and is never printed.
- No continuous polling loop or background service is started.

## Running tests (PowerShell)

    $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
    python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

GitHub Actions runs the same test command. Worker orchestration is covered by fake-adapter tests, including recovery after a simulated lost GitHub POST response. A real end-to-end request remains to be run after actual model Issues are configured.

موافقم. و این نکته‌ای که اضافه کردی مهم‌تر از خودِ گزینهٔ `source_comment_id` است: **Bridge نباید فقط یک صف‌پرداز باشد؛ باید امکان ارسال هدفمند و مستقل درخواست به مدل را هم داشته باشد.**

من این را به‌عنوان یک نیاز معماری در نظر می‌گیرم، نه یک استثنای موقت برای آزمایش Qwen.

پیشنهادم این است که دو مسیر مستقل داشته باشیم:

1. **مسیر صف (Queue):** رفتار فعلی حفظ شود؛ اولویت‌بندی، بازیابی درخواست‌های نیمه‌تمام و ترتیب پردازش طبق قواعد صف.
2. **مسیر مستقیم (Direct):** من بتوانم یک درخواست مشخص را با تعیین مدل مقصد ارسال کنم، بدون اینکه درخواست‌های قدیمی‌تر صف مانع آن شوند.

در مسیر مستقیم، انتخاب درخواست باید صریح باشد؛ مثلاً با شناسهٔ کامنت یا متن تازه‌ای که همان لحظه ارسال می‌کنیم. درخواست‌های دیگر صف نباید جابه‌جا، حذف یا بی‌دلیل تغییر وضعیت داده شوند. همچنین کنترل جلوگیری از پاسخ تکراری GitHub باید پابرجا بماند.

یعنی اختیار انتخاب اینکه «الان کدام درخواست به کدام مدل برود» از منِ ناظر فنی هم قابل استفاده باشد؛ اما اجرای واقعی، فراخوانی مدل و انتشار پاسخ همچنان باید تحت کنترل و اجازهٔ تو بماند.مرور کد فعلی هم نشان داد چرا این قابلیت لازم است: `run_once()` ابتدا هر درخواست `PROCESSING` را انتخاب می‌کند و بعد سراغ صف می‌رود؛ در حال حاضر راهی برای انتخاب شناسهٔ مشخص وجود ندارد.

برای پیاده‌سازی، دو قابلیت را در نظر می‌گیرم:

- `--source-comment-id`: پردازش یک سؤال مشخص از GitHub، حتی اگر درخواست‌های قدیمی‌تری در صف باشند. فقط همان درخواست تغییر وضعیت می‌دهد و پاسخ آن با سازوکار جلوگیری از انتشار تکراری ثبت می‌شود.
- `--prompt`: ارسال یک متن تازه و دلخواه مستقیماً به مدل انتخاب‌شده، بدون ورود به صف و بدون نیاز به ساختن کامنت GitHub.

یک نکته را باید مشخص کنیم: **پاسخ مسیر `--prompt` را فعلاً فقط در ترمینال نمایش بدهیم، یا آن را هم در یک Issue مشخص GitHub منتشر کنیم؟**

پیشنهاد من نمایش محلی به‌صورت پیش‌فرض است؛ انتشار در GitHub بهتر است یک عمل جداگانه و صریح باشد. فعلاً هیچ فایلی را تغییر نداده‌ام و چیزی را به GitHub نفرستاده‌ام.

نه برای همه درخواستهای مشترک یک ایسو جدا ولی طوری توش ثبت بشه تا نام مدل و زمان و بقیه چیزا قابل پیگیری باشه

پس یک **Issue مشترک برای تمام درخواست‌های مستقیم مدل‌ها** می‌سازیم؛ مستقل از Issueهای گفت‌وگوی عادی هر مدل.

عنوان پیشنهادی: `Direct Model Requests`

برای اینکه بعداً بتوانیم هر درخواست را دقیق ردیابی کنیم، پیشنهاد می‌کنم هر درخواست یک شناسهٔ یکتا داشته باشد و اطلاعات زیر در ثبت آن بیاید:

| فیلد | کاربرد |
|---|---|
| Request ID | شناسهٔ یکتای درخواست |
| Model ID و Model Name | مدل انتخاب‌شده و نام واقعی مدل در Ollama |
| Submitted At | زمان ثبت درخواست |
| Started At | زمان شروع اجرای مدل |
| Completed At | زمان پایان اجرا |
| Status | وضعیت: در انتظار، در حال اجرا، موفق یا خطا |
| Prompt | متن درخواست |
| Response | پاسخ مدل |
| Duration | مدت اجرای درخواست |

**یک نکتهٔ معماری:** درخواست مستقیم نباید وارد صف عادی شود یا ترتیب آن را تغییر دهد. همچنین خطای یک درخواست مستقیم نباید وضعیت درخواست‌های صف عادی را دست‌کاری کند.

برای ثبت در GitHub هم می‌توانیم هر درخواست و پاسخ آن را در همان Issue مشترک، با شناسهٔ یکسان و قالب ثابت ثبت کنیم. این‌طوری حتی اگر چند مدل هم‌زمان پاسخ بدهند، سوابقشان با هم اشتباه نمی‌شود.

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .providers.ollama import OllamaChatClient
from .state import BridgeState
from .transport.github_issues import GitHubIssuesTransport
from .worker import BridgeWorker


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="igor-model-bridge",
        description=(

    parser.add_argument(

        help="local TOML configuration file (default: config.toml)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--database", default="bridge-state.sqlite3",
        help="SQLite state file (default: bridge-state.sqlite3)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model-id",
        help="limit this run to one configured model ID",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--execute", action="store_true",
        help="process at most one question and publish its response (requires --model-id)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.execute and not args.model_id:
        parser.error("--execute requires --model-id; this prevents processing other model Issues")

    state: BridgeState | None = None
    try:
        config = load_config(args.config)
        if args.model_id:
            config.model_by_id(args.model_id)

        token = config.github_token()
        github = GitHubIssuesTransport(
            repository=config.repository,
            token=token,
            timeout=20.0,
        )
        ollama = OllamaChatClient(
            base_url=config.ollama_base_url,
            timeout=config.ollama_timeout_seconds,
        )
        state = BridgeState(Path(args.database))
        worker = BridgeWorker(
            config=config,
            state=state,
            github=github,
            ollama=ollama,
        )

        if args.execute:
            result = worker.run_once(model_id=args.model_id)
            print(f"status: {result.status}")
            if result.source_comment_id is not None:
                print(f"source_comment_id: {result.source_comment_id}")
            if result.issue_number is not None:
                print(f"issue_number: {result.issue_number}")
            if result.model_id is not None:
                print(f"model_id: {result.model_id}")
            if result.response_comment_id is not None:
                print(f"response_comment_id: {result.response_comment_id}")
            return 0

        inserted = worker.poll(model_id=args.model_id)
        routes = (
            (config.model_by_id(args.model_id),)
            if args.model_id else config.models
        )
        issue_numbers = {route.issue_number for route in routes}
        visible_items = [
            item for item in state.list_pending_items()
            if item.issue_number in issue_numbers
        ]
        pending = sum(item.status in {"NEW", "RECEIVED", "ERROR", "PROCESSING"} for item in visible_items)
        print("mode: poll-only (no model calls and no GitHub replies)")
        print(f"new_questions: {inserted}")
        print(f"queued_or_unresolved: {pending}")
        for item in visible_items:
            if item.status in {"NEW", "RECEIVED", "ERROR", "PROCESSING"}:
                print(
                    f"- issue=#{item.issue_number} "
                    f"comment={item.source_comment_id} status={item.status}"
                )
        print("To process one question, rerun with --execute --model-id <id>.")
        return 0
    except (KeyError, OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        if state is not None:
            state.close()

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from bridge.config import BridgeConfig, ModelRoute
from bridge.state import BridgeState
from bridge.transport.github_issues import GitHubIssuesTransport
from bridge.worker import BridgeWorker


class FakeGitHub:
    is_igor_question = staticmethod(GitHubIssuesTransport.is_igor_question)
    format_response_comment = staticmethod(GitHubIssuesTransport.format_response_comment)

    def __init__(self):
        self.comments = {11: [], 12: []}
        self.responses = {11: [], 12: []}
        self.next_id = 900
        self.fail_after_publish = False
        self.response_lookups = []

    def list_issue_comments(self, issue_number):
        return list(self.comments[issue_number])

    def find_response_comment(self, issue_number, source_comment_id):
        self.response_lookups.append((issue_number, str(source_comment_id)))
        marker = GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker(source_comment_id)
        return next(
            (c for c in self.responses[issue_number] if marker in c["body"]),
            None,
        )

    def create_issue_comment(self, issue_number, body):
        self.next_id += 1
        created = {"id": self.next_id, "body": body}
        self.responses[issue_number].append(created)
        if self.fail_after_publish:
            self.fail_after_publish = False
            raise RuntimeError("simulated lost HTTP response after GitHub accepted POST")
        return created

    def add_question(self, issue_number, comment_id, body, created_at):
        self.comments[issue_number].append({
            "id": comment_id,
            "created_at": created_at,
            "body": body,
            "user": {"login": "igor-user"},
        })


class FakeOllama:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.answer = "A careful model answer."

    def chat(self, model, messages, *, think=None):
        self.calls.append((model, messages, think))
        return type("Result", (), {"content": self.answer})()


class WorkerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.state = BridgeState(Path(self.temp.name) / "state.sqlite3")
        self.addCleanup(self.state.close)
        self.config = BridgeConfig(
            repository="owner/repo",
            token_env="GITHUB_TOKEN",
            igor_username="igor-user",
            ollama_base_url="http://localhost:11434",
            ollama_timeout_seconds=30,
            models=(
                ModelRoute("qwen", 11, "ollama", "qwen35-local:latest", False),
                ModelRoute("gemma", 12, "ollama", "gemma3:4b"),
            ),
        )
        self.github = FakeGitHub()
        self.ollama = FakeOllama()
        self.worker = BridgeWorker(
            config=self.config,
            state=self.state,
            github=self.github,
            ollama=self.ollama,
        )

    def add_question(self, issue=11, comment_id=101, minute="00"):
        self.github.add_question(
            issue, comment_id, f"Question {comment_id}",
            f"2026-11-13T00:{minute}:00Z",
        )

    def test_poll_filters_and_deduplicates_comments(self):
        self.add_question()
        self.github.comments[11].append({
            "id": 102, "created_at": "2026-11-13T00:01:00Z",
            "body": "not Igor", "user": {"login": "someone-else"},
        })
        self.github.comments[11].append({
            "id": 103, "created_at": "2026-11-13T00:02:00Z",
            "body": "bridge response <!-- igor-model-bridge:response-to=88 -->",
            "user": {"login": "igor-user"},
        })
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.poll(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.poll(), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.state.list_items()), 1)

    def test_processes_oldest_question_and_uses_explicit_issue_route(self):
        self.add_question(comment_id=201, minute="02")
        self.add_question(comment_id=202, minute="01")
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.source_comment_id, "202")
        self.assertEqual(result.model_id, "qwen")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "qwen35-local:latest")
        self.assertIs(self.ollama.calls[0][2], False)
        self.assertIn(
            GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker("202"),
            self.github.responses[11][0]["body"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("202").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("201").status, "NEW")

    def test_routes_second_issue_to_its_configured_model(self):
        self.add_question(issue=12, comment_id=301)
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.model_id, "gemma")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "gemma3:4b")
        self.assertIsNone(self.ollama.calls[0][2])

    def test_reconciles_processing_item_without_calling_ollama(self):
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="401", issue_number=11,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:00:00Z", content="Already answered?",
        )
        self.state.mark_processing("401")
        self.github.responses[11].append({
            "id": 940,
            "body": "Already answered.\n\n"
                    + GitHubIssuesTransport.response_marker("401"),
        })
        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "reconciled")
        self.assertEqual(result.response_comment_id, "940")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("401").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls, [])

    def test_unpublished_interrupted_item_is_retried_before_new_pending_work(self):
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="451", issue_number=11,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:00:00Z", content="Interrupted question",
        )
        self.state.mark_processing("451")
        self.state.enqueue(
            source_comment_id="452", issue_number=12,
            created_at="2026-11-13T00:01:00Z", content="Newer question",
        )

        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.source_comment_id, "451")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "qwen35-local:latest")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("451").status, "RESPONDED")
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("452").status, "NEW")

    def test_retry_after_lost_post_response_reconciles_without_duplicate(self):
        self.add_question(comment_id=501)
        self.github.fail_after_publish = True
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "lost HTTP response"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.responses[11]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("501").status, "ERROR")

        result = self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "reconciled")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.responses[11]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.ollama.calls), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("501").status, "RESPONDED")

    def test_provider_failure_keeps_question_retryable(self):
        class BrokenOllama:
            def chat(self, model, messages, *, think=None):
                raise RuntimeError("temporary model failure")

        self.worker.ollama = BrokenOllama()
        self.add_question(comment_id=601)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "temporary model failure"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("601").status, "ERROR")
        # ERROR retries must also reconcile the remote marker before inference.
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "temporary model failure"):
            self.worker.run_once()
        self.assertEqual(
            self.github.response_lookups,
            [(11, "601"), (11, "601")],
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("601").status, "ERROR")

    def test_single_model_run_does_not_touch_other_issue_queue(self):
        self.add_question(issue=11, comment_id=701)
        self.add_question(issue=12, comment_id=702)
        result = self.worker.run_once(model_id="gemma")

        self.assertEqual(result.status, "responded")
        self.assertEqual(result.issue_number, 12)
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls[0][0], "gemma3:4b")
        self.assertIsNone(self.ollama.calls[0][2])
        self.assertIsNone(self.state.get("701"))
        self.assertEqual(self.state.get("702").status, "RESPONDED")

    def test_idle_when_no_igor_questions_exist(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.worker.run_once().status, "idle")
        self.assertEqual(self.ollama.calls, [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

[L2]   "content": "# Igor Model Bridge

A small, independent bridge between Igor (ChatGPT) and local AI models served by Ollama.

## Status

**Protocol/state foundation, GitHub Issues transport, explicit model routing, Ollama adapter, sequential Worker, and a safe one-shot CLI Runner are implemented.** A real GitHub-to-Ollama round trip has not yet been run. No shell access, code editing, or Ilan integration is enabled.

## First milestone

Run a local bridge process that reads Igor's discussion messages from model-specific GitHub Issues, routes each Issue to its explicitly configured Ollama model, queues questions FIFO, posts correlated responses, and recovers safely after restart.

## Agreed v0 decisions

- One persistent GitHub Issue per model; interview rounds can use an optional interview_id.
- Explicit model routing; never infer a model from an Issue title.
- FIFO queue; no pending question is discarded when a newer one arrives.
- Sequential model execution.
- Persistent deduplication using GitHub comment IDs and SQLite.
- Restart reconciliation using stable response correlation markers.
- The practical guarantee is idempotent response publication, not exactly-once inference.

## Boundaries

- The user is the final authority.
- The bridge is independent of Ilan.
- First transport: GitHub Issues; first provider: Ollama.
- v0 is discussion-only: no tools, shell, workspace access, code changes, or task execution.
- Secrets stay local; never commit tokens.
- Model memory unloading/optimization is deferred.

## Configuration

Requires Python 3.11+ (standard-library tomllib).

1. Copy config.example.toml to config.toml.
2. Set github.igor_username to the GitHub login used by Igor.
3. Create the persistent model Issues and replace each issue_number = 0 with its real Issue number.
4. Set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable locally. The token is never stored in TOML.
5. Load with load_config("config.toml"). Startup validation rejects missing or duplicate mappings.

The example lists four local Ollama tags from the earlier model shortlist. Verify the exact tags on the machine before using them. For Qwen routes, set `think = false` to disable Thinking for that route; omit the setting for non-Qwen models to preserve their default behavior.

## Ollama adapter

The standard-library adapter sends non-streaming POST requests to /api/chat, always with an explicit model tag and stream=false. It accepts only system/user/assistant messages and returns the assistant text plus available usage/timing metadata. HTTP errors, connection failures, invalid JSON, incomplete responses, and empty model output are surfaced as OllamaError.

Example:

    from bridge.config import load_config
    from bridge.providers.ollama import OllamaChatClient

    config = load_config("config.toml")
    route = config.model_by_id("qwen35-local")
    client = OllamaChatClient(
        base_url=config.ollama_base_url,
        timeout=config.ollama_timeout_seconds,
    )
    result = client.chat(
        route.model_name,
        [{"role": "user", "content": "Give a short self-introduction."}],
        think=route.think,
    )
    print(result.content)

The adapter does not execute tools or access files. It does not check that a model tag is installed; Ollama reports that at request time.

## Current layout

igor-model-bridge/
- config.example.toml
- src/bridge/config.py
- src/bridge/providers/ollama.py
- src/bridge/runner.py
- src/bridge/__main__.py
- src/bridge/protocol.py
- src/bridge/state.py
- src/bridge/transport/github_issues.py
- tests/test_config.py
- tests/test_ollama.py
- tests/test_runner.py
- tests/test_protocol.py
- tests/test_state.py
- tests/test_worker.py
- tests/test_github_issues.py

## Running the bridge (PowerShell)

    $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
    python -m bridge --config config.toml --model-id qwen35-local

Only after reviewing the queued comment IDs, explicitly enable one live response:

    python -m bridge --config config.toml --model-id qwen35-local --execute

Safety properties:
- `--execute` requires an explicit `--model-id`; one run processes at most one item from that model's Issue.
- Other model Issues and their queue items are left untouched during a model-scoped run.
- Without `--execute`, the Runner does not call Ollama or create GitHub comments.
- The GitHub token is read from the configured environment variable and is never printed.
- No continuous polling loop or background service is started.

## Running tests (PowerShell)

    $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
    python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

GitHub Actions runs the same test command. Worker orchestration is covered by fake-adapter tests, including recovery after a simulated lost GitHub POST response. A real end-to-end request remains to be run after actual model Issues are configured.

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


VALID_STATUSES = {"NEW", "RECEIVED", "PROCESSING", "RESPONDED", "ERROR"}


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class QueueItem:
    source_comment_id: str
    issue_number: int
    created_at: str
    content: str
    status: str
    response_comment_id: str | None
    error: str | None
    last_error_at: str | None


class BridgeState:
    """Persist source comment IDs and queue status in a local SQLite database.

    The source GitHub comment ID is the idempotency key. Re-polling the same
    comment is safe: enqueue() returns False and does not create another item.
    """

    def __init__(self, database_path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.database_path = str(database_path)
        if self.database_path != ":memory:":
            Path(self.database_path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._connection = sqlite3.connect(self.database_path)
        self._connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        self._connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        self._create_schema()

    def _create_schema(self) -> None:
        with self._connection:
            self._connection.execute(
                """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS queue_items (
                    source_comment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    issue_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                    content TEXT NOT NULL,
                    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
                        status IN ('NEW', 'RECEIVED', 'PROCESSING', 'RESPONDED', 'ERROR')
                    ),
                    response_comment_id TEXT UNIQUE,
                    error TEXT,
                    last_error_at TEXT,
                    inserted_order INTEGER NOT NULL
                )
                """
            )
            columns = {
                row["name"]
                for row in self._connection.execute(
                    "PRAGMA table_info(queue_items)"
                ).fetchall()
            }
            if "last_error_at" not in columns:
                self._connection.execute(
                    "ALTER TABLE queue_items ADD COLUMN last_error_at TEXT"
                )

            # Historical failure times were not stored. Use created_at as a
            # deterministic fallback; the actual failure time is unknown.
            self._connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE queue_items
                SET last_error_at = created_at
                WHERE status = 'ERROR' AND last_error_at IS NULL
                """
            )

            self._connection.execute(
                """
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_queue_pending
                ON queue_items(status, created_at, inserted_order)
                """
            )

    def enqueue(
        self,
        *,
        source_comment_id: str,
        issue_number: int,
        created_at: str,
        content: str,
    ) -> bool:
        """Insert a new pending question; return False if its ID already exists."""
        if not source_comment_id or not source_comment_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("source_comment_id must be non-empty")
        if issue_number <= 0:
            raise ValueError("issue_number must be positive")
        if not created_at or not created_at.strip():
            raise ValueError("created_at must be non-empty")
        if not content or not content.strip():
            raise ValueError("content must be non-empty")

        with self._connection:
            cursor = self._connection.execute(
                """
                INSERT OR IGNORE INTO queue_items
                    (source_comment_id, issue_number, created_at, content, status, inserted_order)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'NEW', (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(inserted_order), 0) + 1
                                            FROM queue_items))
                """,
                (str(source_comment_id), issue_number, created_at, content),
            )
        return cursor.rowcount == 1

    def get_next_pending(self, *, issue_number: int | None = None) -> QueueItem | None:
        """Return the oldest pending item, optionally limited to one Issue."""
        if issue_number is not None and issue_number <= 0:
            raise ValueError("issue_number must be positive")
        query = """
            SELECT * FROM queue_items
            WHERE status IN ('NEW', 'RECEIVED', 'ERROR')
        """
        params: tuple[int, ...] = ()
        if issue_number is not None:
            query += " AND issue_number = ?"
            params = (issue_number,)
        query += """
            ORDER BY
                CASE
                    WHEN status IN ('NEW', 'RECEIVED') THEN 0
                    WHEN status = 'ERROR' THEN 1
                END ASC,
                CASE
                    WHEN status IN ('NEW', 'RECEIVED') THEN created_at
                END ASC,
                CASE
                    WHEN status = 'ERROR' THEN
                        COALESCE(julianday(last_error_at), julianday(created_at))
                END ASC,
                inserted_order ASC
            LIMIT 1
        """
        row = self._connection.execute(query, params).fetchone()
        return self._to_item(row) if row else None

    def get_in_progress(self, *, issue_number: int | None = None) -> QueueItem | None:
        """Return the oldest interrupted item, optionally limited to one Issue."""
        if issue_number is not None and issue_number <= 0:
            raise ValueError("issue_number must be positive")
        query = "SELECT * FROM queue_items WHERE status = 'PROCESSING'"
        params: tuple[int, ...] = ()
        if issue_number is not None:
            query += " AND issue_number = ?"
            params = (issue_number,)
        query += " ORDER BY created_at ASC, inserted_order ASC LIMIT 1"
        row = self._connection.execute(query, params).fetchone()
        return self._to_item(row) if row else None

    def mark_processing(self, source_comment_id: str) -> None:
        self._set_status(source_comment_id, "PROCESSING", error=None)

    def mark_responded(
        self, source_comment_id: str, response_comment_id: str
    ) -> None:
        if not response_comment_id or not response_comment_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("response_comment_id must be non-empty")
        with self._connection:
            cursor = self._connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE queue_items
                SET status = 'RESPONDED', response_comment_id = ?, error = NULL,
                    last_error_at = NULL
                WHERE source_comment_id = ?
                """,
                (str(response_comment_id), str(source_comment_id)),
            )
            if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                raise KeyError(f"Unknown source comment ID: {source_comment_id}")

    def mark_error(self, source_comment_id: str, error: str) -> None:
        if not error or not error.strip():
            raise ValueError("error must be non-empty")
        with self._connection:
            cursor = self._connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE queue_items
                SET status = 'ERROR', error = ?, last_error_at = ?
                WHERE source_comment_id = ?
                """,
                (
                    error,
                    datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"),
                    str(source_comment_id),
                ),
            )
            if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                raise KeyError(f"Unknown source comment ID: {source_comment_id}")

    def get(self, source_comment_id: str) -> QueueItem | None:
        row = self._connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM queue_items WHERE source_comment_id = ?",
            (str(source_comment_id),),
        ).fetchone()
        return self._to_item(row) if row else None

    def list_items(self) -> list[QueueItem]:
        rows = self._connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM queue_items ORDER BY created_at ASC, inserted_order ASC"
        ).fetchall()
        return [self._to_item(row) for row in rows]

    def list_pending_items(self) -> list[QueueItem]:
        """List unresolved items in the same order that run_once() processes them.

        Interrupted PROCESSING items come first, followed by NEW/RECEIVED
        questions in FIFO order, then ERROR items by their most recent failure.
        """
        rows = self._connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT * FROM queue_items
            WHERE status IN ('PROCESSING', 'NEW', 'RECEIVED', 'ERROR')
            ORDER BY
                CASE
                    WHEN status = 'PROCESSING' THEN 0
                    WHEN status IN ('NEW', 'RECEIVED') THEN 1
                    WHEN status = 'ERROR' THEN 2
                END ASC,
                CASE
                    WHEN status IN ('PROCESSING', 'NEW', 'RECEIVED')
                    THEN created_at
                END ASC,
                CASE
                    WHEN status = 'ERROR'
                    THEN COALESCE(julianday(last_error_at), julianday(created_at))
                END ASC,
                inserted_order ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()
        return [self._to_item(row) for row in rows]

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._connection.close()

    def __enter__(self) -> "BridgeState":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:
        self.close()

    def _set_status(
        self, source_comment_id: str, status: str, *, error: str | None
    ) -> None:
        if status not in VALID_STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status: {status}")
        with self._connection:
            cursor = self._connection.execute(
                "UPDATE queue_items SET status = ?, error = ? WHERE source_comment_id = ?",
                (status, error, str(source_comment_id)),
            )
            if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                raise KeyError(f"Unknown source comment ID: {source_comment_id}")

    @staticmethod
    def _to_item(row: sqlite3.Row) -> QueueItem:
        return QueueItem(
            source_comment_id=row["source_comment_id"],
            issue_number=row["issue_number"],
            created_at=row["created_at"],
            content=row["content"],
            status=row["status"],
            response_comment_id=row["response_comment_id"],
            error=row["error"],
            last_error_at=row["last_error_at"],
        )

طرح پایه‌ای که مبنای کار قرار می‌دهم:

1. **ورودی مستقیم:** دریافت متن درخواست و `model_id`؛ بدون نیاز به ساختن کامنت ورودی در Issue عادی مدل.
2. **اجرای مستقل:** فراخوانی مستقیم مدل انتخاب‌شده در Ollama؛ بدون پردازش یا جابه‌جایی هیچ‌کدام از آیتم‌های صف.
3. **ثبت در Issue #5:** ثبت درخواست و پاسخ با یک `request_id` مشترک و اطلاعات مدل، زمان ثبت، شروع و پایان، وضعیت و مدت اجرا.
4. **خطا و بازیابی:** اگر اجرا شکست خورد، وضعیت همان درخواست `ERROR` ثبت شود؛ خطای آن نباید صف عادی را تغییر دهد.
5. **کنترل اجرا:** اجرای مدل و انتشار نتیجه در GitHub همچنان نیازمند اجازهٔ صریح توست.

با بررسی کد فعلی مخزن، چند نکتهٔ اجرایی مهم مشخص شد:

### طراحی دقیق‌تر

**۱. تنظیمات**

شمارهٔ Issue مقصد در `config.toml` ثبت می‌شود:

```toml
[github]
direct_issue_number = 5
```

Bridge فقط از Issue موجود استفاده می‌کند؛ ساخت Issue جدید در کارش نیست.

**۲. ثبت هر درخواست**

## Selection 1
یک تصمیم کوچک ولی مهم را هم باید قبل از پیاده‌سازی روشن کنیم: برای درخواست مستقیمی که وسط اجرای مدل قطع می‌شود، ترجیح می‌دهم Bridge آن را خودکار دوباره اجرا نکند؛ آن را INTERRUPTED علامت بزند و منتظر دستور صریح برای ادامه بماند. این کار احتمال اجرای دوباره و هزینهٔ محاسباتی ناخواسته را کاهش می‌دهد. آیا با این رفتار موافقی؟

## My request:
موافقم با این کار خودت مدیریت درخواست های ناموفق ام انجام میدی

موافقم. این مسئولیت را در طراحی Bridge به عهدهٔ من می‌گذاریم؛ اما باید بین **مدیریت خطا** و **اجازهٔ اجرای مجدد مدل** تفاوت بگذاریم.

از این به بعد رفتار موردنظر چنین است:

1. اگر درخواست موفق شود، نتیجه در Issue شمارهٔ ۵ ثبت می‌شود.
2. اگر مدل خطا بدهد، درخواست `ERROR` می‌شود و علت خطا ثبت خواهد شد.
3. اگر اجرای Bridge ناگهان قطع شود و نتیجه نامشخص بماند، درخواست `INTERRUPTED` می‌شود.
4. من درخواست‌های ناموفق را بررسی، دسته‌بندی و علت‌یابی می‌کنم و راه اصلاح را پیشنهاد می‌دهم.
5. **اجرای مجدد مدل خودکار نیست**؛ پس از بررسی، برای Retry یا ادامهٔ اجرا از تو اجازه می‌گیرم.
6. درخواست‌های ناموفق هرگز بی‌صدا حذف نمی‌شوند یا به صف عادی منتقل نمی‌شوند.

یک نکتهٔ مهم: اگر GitHub پاسخ را ثبت کرده باشد ولی Bridge پاسخ تأیید را دریافت نکرده باشد، ابتدا نتیجهٔ قبلی را جست‌وجو می‌کنیم تا پاسخ تکراری منتشر نشود.

این یعنی من مسئول پیگیری و مدیریت چرخهٔ خطا هستم، ولی اختیار مصرف منابع و اجرای مجدد بدون اجازهٔ تو را ندارم.

**این تصمیم را در طراحی تثبیت می‌کنیم.** گام بعدی، با اجازهٔ تو، شروع تغییرات محلی و تست آن‌هاست؛ هنوز چیزی را تغییر نداده‌ام.

[L2]   "content": "# Architecture — Igor Model Bridge (v0)

## Purpose and scope

A controlled communication path between Igor (ChatGPT) and local Ollama models. v0 supports DISCUSSION messages only. Explicitly excluded: shell/tool calls, workspace/file access, code modification, task execution, autonomous model-to-model conversation, and Ilan integration.

## Components

- Protocol core: provider- and transport-neutral message envelope.
- GitHub Issues transport: reads comments, filters Igor questions, posts correlated responses.
- Configuration: validates repository, Igor login, token environment variable name, Ollama endpoint/timeout, and model routing.
- Ollama provider: sends non-streaming chat requests and validates responses.
- Worker: polls configured Issues, ingests eligible comments, and processes one FIFO item per run in sequence. Supports a model-scoped run so the first live test cannot consume another model's queue. Before every inference attempt it checks GitHub for an existing correlated response.
- Runner: safe one-shot CLI. Default is poll-only; live inference and publication require explicit `--execute` plus a selected `--model-id`. No daemon or continuous loop.
- Local state: durable SQLite processing records.

## Explicit model routing

Each route has a stable model_id, positive issue_number, provider, and exact provider model tag. Model IDs and Issue numbers must be unique. Unknown Issue numbers never fall back to a default model. v0 accepts only provider = "ollama". Issue titles are human-readable only and are not authoritative routing metadata.

There is one persistent Issue per local model. An optional interview_id can distinguish interview rounds within that Issue.

The example config uses issue_number = 0 as an intentional unconfigured placeholder. The loader rejects it; real Issue numbers must be supplied before startup.

## Configuration and secrets

TOML is parsed with Python 3.11+'s standard-library tomllib. Copy config.example.toml to the local, untracked config.toml. The GitHub token is read only from the environment variable named by github.token_env. The token is not stored in TOML or retained in BridgeConfig.

The loader validates required values, repository format, HTTP(S) Ollama URL, positive timeout, positive Issue numbers, provider support, and duplicate model IDs/Issue numbers. It does not contact GitHub or Ollama; connectivity checks belong to their adapters.

## Ollama chat adapter

- Uses Python's standard-library urllib and JSON; no additional runtime package is required.
- Sends POST /api/chat with stream=false and the exact configured model tag.
- Accepts only system, user, and assistant message roles. Tool roles and tool execution are intentionally unsupported.
- Supports optional Ollama generation options.
- Returns assistant text and optional timing/token-count metadata.
- Converts HTTP errors, URL/timeout failures, invalid JSON, empty content, and incomplete responses into OllamaError.
- The adapter performs no filesystem, shell, or tool operations and does not infer or select model tags.
- Model installation is not preflighted; Ollama reports an unknown model at request time.

## Queue and recovery invariants

- Eligible Igor comments enter a FIFO queue and are never silently discarded.
- One model request runs at a time.
- GitHub comment IDs are source identities; SQLite persists state.
- On restart, reconcile PROCESSING records against GitHub response markers before retrying.
- A response comment is not marked complete until confirmed on GitHub.
- Publication is idempotent across the crash window after remote publication; inference may repeat if a generated answer was not published.

## Security and authority

The GitHub token stays local and is never placed in source, committed config, prompts, or Issue content. Only the configured Igor identity is eligible input. Model output is untrusted data. The bridge grants models no execution tools. User is the final authority.

## Implementation status

Implemented: protocol envelope and validation; timezone-aware timestamps; SQLite FIFO queue and deduplication; GitHub Issues comment listing/publication and correlation markers; validated TOML routing; environment-only token lookup; Ollama non-streaming chat adapter and unit tests; CI.

Not implemented: worker orchestration; end-to-end recovery/integration test; real Ollama/GitHub round trip.

## Next steps

1. Worker integration and restart-recovery tests.
2. Harmless end-to-end test using one configured model Issue.
3. Sequential model interview workflow.
4. Additional providers only if needed.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6abd43baafe081918bfcee9d948b3ed3/update_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"retashop2020-boop/igor-model-bridge","path":"ARCHITECTURE.md","content":"# Architecture — Igor Model Bridge (v0)

## Purpose and scope

A controlled communication path between Igor (ChatGPT) and local Ollama models. The current v0 supports discussion requests only. It does not grant models shell/tool calls, workspace/file access, code modification, task execution, or autonomous model-to-model conversation. Ilan integration is out of scope for this version.

The Bridge has two deliberately separate execution paths:

1. **Queue execution** — handles incoming model-Issue comments according to durable queue priority and recovery rules.
2. **Direct execution** — lets an explicitly selected request reach a chosen model without being blocked by unrelated older queue entries.

These paths must not silently reorder, consume, or mutate one another's work.

## Components

- Protocol core: provider- and transport-neutral message envelope.
- GitHub Issues transport: reads comments, filters Igor questions, posts correlated responses, and supports the shared direct-request log.
- Configuration: validates repository, Igor login, token environment variable name, Ollama endpoint/timeout, model routing, and (for direct mode) the shared destination Issue.
- Ollama provider: sends non-streaming chat requests and validates responses.
- Worker: polls configured model Issues, ingests eligible comments, and processes at most one queue item per run. It supports a model-scoped run. Before inference it checks GitHub for an existing correlated response.
- Runner: safe one-shot CLI. Default is poll-only; queue inference/publication requires explicit `--execute` and a selected `--model-id`. Direct execution is a separate explicit CLI path.
- Local state: durable SQLite records for queue items and, when direct mode is implemented, a separate direct-request ledger.

## Explicit model routing

Each model route has a stable `model_id`, positive `issue_number`, provider, and exact provider model tag. Model IDs and model-Issue numbers must be unique. Unknown Issue numbers never fall back to a default model. v0 accepts only provider = "ollama". Issue titles are human-readable only and are not authoritative routing metadata.

There is one persistent input Issue per local model. An optional `interview_id` can distinguish interview rounds within that Issue.

The example config uses `issue_number = 0` as an intentional unconfigured placeholder. The loader rejects it; real Issue numbers must be supplied before startup.

## Queue execution and recovery invariants

- Eligible Igor comments enter a durable queue and are never silently discarded.
- One model request runs at a time.
- GitHub comment IDs are source identities; SQLite persists processing state.
- Queue priority is:
  1. existing `PROCESSING` items first (oldest first), so interrupted work can be reconciled;
  2. new/received items next, FIFO by creation/insertion order;
  3. `ERROR` items last, ordered by `last_error_at`, with creation time and insertion order as tie-breakers.
- `ERROR` items remain visible and recoverable; they are not silently deleted or automatically promoted ahead of new questions.
- Before retrying an item already marked `PROCESSING`, reconcile its source comment against GitHub response markers.
- A response is not marked complete until its publication is confirmed on GitHub.
- The correlation marker prevents duplicate response comments if a GitHub POST succeeded but its acknowledgement was lost.
- The queue worker processes no more than one item per run.
- Queue execution retains its own ordering and recovery behavior; direct execution must not poll the queue as a side effect.

## Direct execution — approved design, implementation pending

### Purpose

Direct execution exists for Igor to select a particular request and send it to a chosen model even when older queue items are waiting or in error. It is a separate path, not a queue-priority override.

### Supported request forms

- **Selected source comment:** execute one existing GitHub source comment by its exact `source_comment_id`, with an explicit `model_id`. The comment must belong to the Issue configured for that model. This path must not poll the queue or process any other item. Only the selected queue record may have its state changed.
- **Fresh prompt:** send a new prompt directly to an explicitly selected `model_id`, without creating or consuming a normal queue item.

The intended CLI selector for the first form is `--source-comment-id <id>`; the fresh-prompt form uses `--prompt <text>`. These selectors and the direct worker path are design targets, not yet implemented.

### Shared destination and audit trail

- All direct requests use the user-created shared Issue **#5 — Direct Model Requests** in this repository: https://github.com/retashop2020-boop/igor-model-bridge/issues/5
- The Bridge must not create this Issue automatically.
- The intended configuration key is `[github].direct_issue_number = 5`. It is not yet implemented in the configuration loader.
- Each direct request gets a stable unique `request_id` and a traceable record containing, at minimum, request type, selected model ID/tag, source comment ID when applicable, prompt, start/end timestamps, status, response or error, duration, and destination comment ID.
- Use one GitHub comment per direct request: create it in a `PROCESSING` state with request metadata, then update that same comment to its terminal state and include the response or error. Do not create separate start and finish comments for one request.
- Persist direct-request state in a dedicated SQLite table, separate from `queue_items`. The ledger and GitHub record must be reconciled using the stable `request_id`.

### Failure and interruption policy

- `ERROR` means the operation failed with a known error.
- `INTERRUPTED` means the Bridge stopped while a direct request was in flight and the final model outcome may be unknown.
- Direct requests must not be silently discarded, moved into the normal queue, or automatically retried after an error or interruption.
- Igor is responsible for inspecting and classifying failed direct requests, explaining the likely cause, and proposing a recovery action. A retry or resume requires the user's explicit approval.
- If a remote GitHub create/update may have succeeded despite a lost acknowledgement, reconcile by `request_id` before attempting another write.
- Exactly-once inference cannot be guaranteed across a process crash: the model may have completed after the last durable local checkpoint. The safe default is to record `INTERRUPTED` and wait for an explicit decision, rather than silently run the prompt again.

## Configuration and secrets

TOML is parsed with Python 3.11+'s standard-library `tomllib`. Copy `config.example.toml` to the local, untracked `config.toml`. The GitHub token is read only from the environment variable named by `github.token_env`. The token is not stored in TOML or retained in `BridgeConfig`.

The loader validates required values, repository format, HTTP(S) Ollama URL, positive timeout, positive Issue numbers, provider support, and duplicate model IDs/Issue numbers. It does not contact GitHub or Ollama; connectivity checks belong to their adapters. The direct destination Issue setting is part of the approved design but has not yet been added to the loader.

## Ollama chat adapter

- Uses Python's standard-library `urllib` and JSON; no additional runtime package is required.
- Sends POST `/api/chat` with `stream=false` and the exact configured model tag.
- Accepts only system, user, and assistant message roles. Tool roles and tool execution are intentionally unsupported.
- Supports optional Ollama generation options, including the configured thinking behavior.
- Returns assistant text and optional timing/token-count metadata.
- Converts HTTP errors, URL/timeout failures, invalid JSON, empty content, and incomplete responses into `OllamaError`.
- The adapter performs no filesystem, shell, or tool operations and does not infer or select model tags.
- Model installation is not preflighted; Ollama reports an unknown model at request time.

## Security and authority

[L2]   "content": "# Architecture — Igor Model Bridge (v0)

## Purpose and scope

A controlled communication path between Igor (ChatGPT) and local Ollama models. The current v0 supports discussion requests only. It does not grant models shell/tool calls, workspace/file access, code modification, task execution, or autonomous model-to-model conversation. Ilan integration is out of scope for this version.

The Bridge has two deliberately separate execution paths:

1. **Queue execution** — handles incoming model-Issue comments according to durable queue priority and recovery rules.
2. **Direct execution** — lets an explicitly selected request reach a chosen model without being blocked by unrelated older queue entries.

These paths must not silently reorder, consume, or mutate one another's work.

## Components

- Protocol core: provider- and transport-neutral message envelope.
- GitHub Issues transport: reads comments, filters Igor questions, posts correlated responses, and supports the shared direct-request log.
- Configuration: validates repository, Igor login, token environment variable name, Ollama endpoint/timeout, model routing, and (for direct mode) the shared destination Issue.
- Ollama provider: sends non-streaming chat requests and validates responses.
- Worker: polls configured model Issues, ingests eligible comments, and processes at most one queue item per run. It supports a model-scoped run. Before inference it checks GitHub for an existing correlated response.
- Runner: safe one-shot CLI. Default is poll-only; queue inference/publication requires explicit `--execute` and a selected `--model-id`. Direct execution is a separate explicit CLI path.
- Local state: durable SQLite records for queue items and, when direct mode is implemented, a separate direct-request ledger.

## Explicit model routing

Each model route has a stable `model_id`, positive `issue_number`, provider, and exact provider model tag. Model IDs and model-Issue numbers must be unique. Unknown Issue numbers never fall back to a default model. v0 accepts only provider = "ollama". Issue titles are human-readable only and are not authoritative routing metadata.

There is one persistent input Issue per local model. An optional `interview_id` can distinguish interview rounds within that Issue.

The example config uses `issue_number = 0` as an intentional unconfigured placeholder. The loader rejects it; real Issue numbers must be supplied before startup.

## Queue execution and recovery invariants

- Eligible Igor comments enter a durable queue and are never silently discarded.
- One model request runs at a time.
- GitHub comment IDs are source identities; SQLite persists processing state.
- Queue priority is:
  1. existing `PROCESSING` items first (oldest first), so interrupted work can be reconciled;
  2. new/received items next, FIFO by creation/insertion order;
  3. `ERROR` items last, ordered by `last_error_at`, with creation time and insertion order as tie-breakers.
- `ERROR` items remain visible and recoverable; they are not silently deleted or automatically promoted ahead of new questions.
- Before retrying an item already marked `PROCESSING`, reconcile its source comment against GitHub response markers.
- A response is not marked complete until its publication is confirmed on GitHub.
- The correlation marker prevents duplicate response comments if a GitHub POST succeeded but its acknowledgement was lost.
- The queue worker processes no more than one item per run.
- Queue execution retains its own ordering and recovery behavior; direct execution must not poll the queue as a side effect.

## Direct execution — approved design, implementation pending

### Purpose

Direct execution exists for Igor to select a particular request and send it to a chosen model even when older queue items are waiting or in error. It is a separate path, not a queue-priority override.

### Supported request forms

- **Selected source comment:** execute one existing GitHub source comment by its exact `source_comment_id`, with an explicit `model_id`. The comment must belong to the Issue configured for that model. This path must not poll the queue or process any other item. Only the selected queue record may have its state changed.
- **Fresh prompt:** send a new prompt directly to an explicitly selected `model_id`, without creating or consuming a normal queue item.

The intended CLI selector for the first form is `--source-comment-id <id>`; the fresh-prompt form uses `--prompt <text>`. These selectors and the direct worker path are design targets, not yet implemented.

### Shared destination and audit trail

- All direct requests use the user-created shared Issue **#5 — Direct Model Requests** in this repository: https://github.com/retashop2020-boop/igor-model-bridge/issues/5
- The Bridge must not create this Issue automatically.
- The intended configuration key is `[github].direct_issue_number = 5`. It is not yet implemented in the configuration loader.
- Each direct request gets a stable unique `request_id` and a traceable record containing, at minimum, request type, selected model ID/tag, source comment ID when applicable, prompt, start/end timestamps, status, response or error, duration, and destination comment ID.
- Use one GitHub comment per direct request: create it in a `PROCESSING` state with request metadata, then update that same comment to its terminal state and include the response or error. Do not create separate start and finish comments for one request.
- Persist direct-request state in a dedicated SQLite table, separate from `queue_items`. The ledger and GitHub record must be reconciled using the stable `request_id`.

### Failure and interruption policy

- `ERROR` means the operation failed with a known error.
- `INTERRUPTED` means the Bridge stopped while a direct request was in flight and the final model outcome may be unknown.
- Direct requests must not be silently discarded, moved into the normal queue, or automatically retried after an error or interruption.
- Igor is responsible for inspecting and classifying failed direct requests, explaining the likely cause, and proposing a recovery action. A retry or resume requires the user's explicit approval.
- If a remote GitHub create/update may have succeeded despite a lost acknowledgement, reconcile by `request_id` before attempting another write.
- Exactly-once inference cannot be guaranteed across a process crash: the model may have completed after the last durable local checkpoint. The safe default is to record `INTERRUPTED` and wait for an explicit decision, rather than silently run the prompt again.

## Configuration and secrets

TOML is parsed with Python 3.11+'s standard-library `tomllib`. Copy `config.example.toml` to the local, untracked `config.toml`. The GitHub token is read only from the environment variable named by `github.token_env`. The token is not stored in TOML or retained in `BridgeConfig`.

The loader validates required values, repository format, HTTP(S) Ollama URL, positive timeout, positive Issue numbers, provider support, and duplicate model IDs/Issue numbers. It does not contact GitHub or Ollama; connectivity checks belong to their adapters. The direct destination Issue setting is part of the approved design but has not yet been added to the loader.

## Ollama chat adapter

- Uses Python's standard-library `urllib` and JSON; no additional runtime package is required.
- Sends POST `/api/chat` with `stream=false` and the exact configured model tag.
- Accepts only system, user, and assistant message roles. Tool roles and tool execution are intentionally unsupported.
- Supports optional Ollama generation options, including the configured thinking behavior.
- Returns assistant text and optional timing/token-count metadata.
- Converts HTTP errors, URL/timeout failures, invalid JSON, empty content, and incomplete responses into `OllamaError`.
- The adapter performs no filesystem, shell, or tool operations and does not infer or select model tags.
- Model installation is not preflighted; Ollama reports an unknown model at request time.

## Security and authority

The GitHub token stays local and is never placed in source, committed config, prompts, or Issue content. Only the configured Igor identity is eligible input. Model output is untrusted data. The Bridge grants models no execution tools. The user is the final authority.

A direct execution request must identify the target model and request explicitly. The existence of a direct path does not grant background/autonomous execution authority. Actual model calls and publication remain subject to the user's explicit execution approval. Ilan has no spending authority.

## Implementation status

### Implemented

- Protocol envelope and validation; timezone-aware timestamps.
- SQLite queue, deduplication, and unresolved-item listing.
- Queue priority and error ordering described above.
- GitHub Issues comment listing/publication and correlation markers.
- Validated TOML model routing and environment-only token lookup.
- Ollama non-streaming chat adapter and unit tests.
- One-shot Runner and Worker queue orchestration.
- Queue/Runner tests and failure-path tests.
- Model-scoped execution and poll-only mode.
- GitHub Actions test workflow.

### Verified in local testing

- The selected state/runner test set passed: 18 tests.
- A real Qwen 3.5 9B request completed through the Bridge and its answer was published to model Issue #1.
- A follow-up Qwen request exceeded the then-configured 120-second Bridge timeout. The same prompt completed through a direct Ollama API test in about 165 seconds. The local, untracked config timeout was then increased to 300 seconds.
- The follow-up answer was obtained locally from Ollama; it was not published through the Bridge.
- There are unresolved queue items in `ERROR`; they must remain visible and must not be retried without an explicit decision.

### Not yet implemented

- Direct execution by `source_comment_id`.
- Direct execution of a fresh `--prompt`.
- Dedicated `direct_requests` SQLite ledger and request lifecycle.
- Configuration for shared direct destination Issue #5.
- Create/update/reconcile of one audit comment per direct request.
- Direct-path interruption and recovery tests.
- End-to-end tests for the complete direct path.

## Next steps

1. Implement direct execution as a separate Worker/Runner path, without queue polling or unrelated queue mutation.
2. Add the direct-request ledger, stable request IDs, and the shared Issue #5 audit trail.
3. Add validation for exact source-comment/model ownership and fresh-prompt input.
4. Add tests for isolation from queue ordering, ERROR/INTERRUPTED states, crash windows, and GitHub write reconciliation.
5. Run local unit tests before any live model call.
6. Perform one harmless direct request only after the user explicitly approves that live execution.
7. Continue sequential model evaluation, one model at a time, after the direct path is stable.
8. Consider additional providers or Ilan integration only as later, separately approved scope.

"""Validated local configuration for Igor Model Bridge (Python 3.11+)."""
from __future__ import annotations
import os
import re
import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

_REPOSITORY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$")
_ENV_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelRoute:
    model_id: str
    issue_number: int
    provider: str
    model_name: str
    think: bool | None = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BridgeConfig:
    repository: str
    token_env: str
    igor_username: str
    ollama_base_url: str
    ollama_timeout_seconds: float
    models: tuple[ModelRoute, ...]

    def model_for_issue(self, issue_number: int) -> ModelRoute:
        for route in self.models:
            if route.issue_number == issue_number:
                return route
        raise KeyError(f"No model route configured for Issue #{issue_number}")

    def model_by_id(self, model_id: str) -> ModelRoute:
        for route in self.models:
            if route.model_id == model_id:
                return route
        raise KeyError(f"No model route configured for model_id {model_id!r}")

    def github_token(self, environ: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
        source = os.environ if environ is None else environ
        token = source.get(self.token_env, "").strip()
        if not token:
            raise ValueError(f"GitHub token environment variable {self.token_env!r} is not set")
        return token

def load_config(path: str | Path) -> BridgeConfig:
    config_path = Path(path)
    try:
        with config_path.open("rb") as stream:
            raw = tomllib.load(stream)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Configuration file not found: {config_path}") from exc
    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid TOML configuration: {exc}") from exc

    github = _require_table(raw, "github")
    ollama = _require_table(raw, "ollama")
    repository = _required_string(github, "repository")
    if not _REPOSITORY_RE.fullmatch(repository):
        raise ValueError("github.repository must use 'owner/name' format")
    token_env = _required_string(github, "token_env")
    if not _ENV_NAME_RE.fullmatch(token_env):
        raise ValueError("github.token_env must be a valid environment variable name")
    igor_username = _required_string(github, "igor_username")

    base_url = _required_string(ollama, "base_url").rstrip("/")
    parsed_url = urlparse(base_url)
    if parsed_url.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or not parsed_url.netloc:
        raise ValueError("ollama.base_url must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL")
    timeout = ollama.get("timeout_seconds", 120)
    if isinstance(timeout, bool) or not isinstance(timeout, (int, float)) or timeout <= 0:
        raise ValueError("ollama.timeout_seconds must be a positive number")

    raw_models = raw.get("models")
    if not isinstance(raw_models, list) or not raw_models:
        raise ValueError("At least one [[models]] route must be configured")
    routes: list[ModelRoute] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    seen_issues: set[int] = set()
    for index, item in enumerate(raw_models, start=1):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"models entry {index} must be a table")
        model_id = _required_string(item, "id", f"models entry {index}")
        provider = _required_string(item, "provider", f"models entry {index}")
        model_name = _required_string(item, "model", f"models entry {index}")
        think = item.get("think")
        if think is not None and not isinstance(think, bool):
            raise ValueError(f"models entry {index}: think must be true or false")
        if think is False and not model_name.lower().startswith("qwen"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"models entry {index}: think = false is reserved for Qwen model tags"
            )
        issue_number = item.get("issue_number")
        if isinstance(issue_number, bool) or not isinstance(issue_number, int) or issue_number <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"models entry {index}: issue_number must be a positive integer; replace the example value with a real GitHub Issue number")
        if provider != "ollama":
            raise ValueError(f"models entry {index}: unsupported provider {provider!r}; v0 supports 'ollama'")
        if model_id in seen_ids:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate model id: {model_id!r}")
        if issue_number in seen_issues:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate GitHub Issue number: {issue_number}")
        seen_ids.add(model_id)
        seen_issues.add(issue_number)
        routes.append(ModelRoute(model_id, issue_number, provider, model_name, think))

    return BridgeConfig(repository, token_env, igor_username, base_url, float(timeout), tuple(routes))

def _require_table(raw: dict, name: str) -> dict:
    value = raw.get(name)
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Missing or invalid [{name}] section")
    return value

def _required_string(table: dict, key: str, section: str = "configuration") -> str:
    value = table.get(key)
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{section}: {key} must be a non-empty string")
    return value.strip()
